items.what: The client-clock pump (advance T at 60 Hz, fire due tickers, drain pending C_Timer.After entries, run shown frames' OnUpdate) is a second copy of tests/activity_ui.lua:13-25 `advance`. Both reach into ui_client.lua's private C_Timer stub shape (`pending[i].at/fn`, `ticker.next/every/cancelled/fn`, `frames[i].scripts.OnUpdate`) defined at tests/ui_client.lua:722-735. Canonical home: tests/ui_client.lua, next to the C_Timer stub it drains.
items.why: Read both: identical loop structure and field names; the only difference is activity_ui counting callbacks (intentional, it asserts idle cost). A change to the C_Timer/ticker stub fields in ui_client.lua must be mirrored in both drivers. Other UI checks (search_ui.lua:89, api_ui.lua:29, tracker_ui.lua:38, waypoint_ui.lua:30) write their own narrower ticks, so ui_client provides no shared pump today.

items.quote: assert(pending <= #distributions * 2 * routes, "queued routes must be deduplicated")
items.what: The dedupe assertion cannot fail: Sync.lua's queue items key entries by routeID, so each batch holds at most `routes` entries, and line 131 has already asserted #queue <= 10 = #distributions * 2. The bound follows arithmetically from the previous assert, so route deduplication is never observed.
items.why: Mutation probe (in memory, via a loadfile wrapper): replacing `pending.entries[routeID] = entry` in Send with a unique non-route key (no dedupe) leaves `luajit tests/sync_spec.lua` printing `sync_spec: ok`. Queue boundedness stays covered by the #queue and #timers asserts; per-route deduplication is uncovered and needs a real check, e.g. that after N Share(id) calls for one route a batch holds one entry for it, or that the total sent entries match the distinct routes.

items.quote:
eventRegistry:TriggerEvent("EditMode.Enter")
	check(host.shown == false, "private tracker hides while Edit Mode owns native slot")
items.what: The Edit Mode step checks only that the host hides. It never drains the Layout queued by EditMode.Enter while Edit Mode is still active, so Layout's Edit Mode guard (which stops the host from restacking or resizing ObjectiveTrackerFrame while Edit Mode owns it) is never exercised.
items.why: In-memory mutation: replacing TrackerHost.lua:216 `if EditModeManagerFrame and ... IsEditModeActive() then` with `if false then` still gives `tracker_host_spec: 32 checks passed`. The timer queued on Enter only runs after editMode.active=false and EditMode.Exit, so the guarded branch is never reached. A drain() with a native.point/height assertion between Enter and Exit would cover it.
